turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Good afternoon, Adrian. Clara Chen speaking. It is good to hear from you. I have time to speak, and we can work through the papers at your pace. If you are at your office, please make yourself comfortable before we begin. There is no need to keep moving between your desk and a meeting room while we talk. Would you prefer me to speak slowly while you arrange what you have in front of you, or are you already settled somewhere quiet?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Hello, Clara. I am in the small room behind my office, so this should be reasonably quiet. I have put my mobile on silent, although someone may knock if a delivery needs attention. 我把本子和信件都带进来了，只是桌子有点小，摊开以后不太整齐。平时我自己看得懂，跟别人讲的时候才发现顺序很乱。 Before we get into the notes, I have the personal particulars here. [[EV_011]] [[EV_012]]

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Thank you. We can leave some space for interruptions rather than trying to rush through everything. A small desk can make an orderly folder look quite different once all the pages are open. You might find it easier to keep the notebook in front of you and leave the loose correspondence to the side until you need it. I will allow you time to find the relevant page. You mentioned that you wanted to work through your investment notes, so please start wherever your current notes begin.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: That is helpful. The difficulty is that I write personal things in the same book as reminders about the business. A supplier calls, I turn a page, then I come back to something I was considering at home. 我没有特意把两边分开，所以有些标题看起来像是最近写的，其实只是后来补上去的。 Let me look at the entry with the folded corner. [[EV_013]] I have a letter underneath the book as well, but I should probably stop shuffling everything while I am reading.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: We can pause while you put the loose letter somewhere it will not obscure the notebook. It is often the physical arrangement that causes trouble during a telephone conversation: the page you need ends up under the page you have just put down. I will keep the conversation unhurried. If you find that the notebook runs from business matters into personal correspondence without a clear break, take a moment to establish where you are on the page before carrying on. You do not need to talk while you are searching.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: [[EV_014]] There, that is exactly the sort of thing I was worried about with this notebook. 我以为折起来的地方就是现在要看的地方，结果旁边夹着的是以前收到的信。我太习惯凭纸张的位置来记事情，不习惯先看标题。 In the office I usually know a document by the colour of the folder or by whose handwriting is on the envelope. That works until somebody tidies my desk and puts the envelopes in a different order.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Please take the time you need to separate the pages. We do not have to fill every pause with conversation, especially while you are looking closely at handwritten material. You can move the older correspondence away from the notebook if that makes the desk easier to use. A folded corner is a useful reminder only while you remember why you folded it, and that can be difficult when the same book travels between your office and home. I am here when you are ready to continue.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I have found the page behind it now. [[EV_015]] Let me put a blank sheet over the older writing so I am not distracted by it. 这样清楚多了。我不是故意绕来绕去，只是平时这些想法都留在自己的本子里，很少需要按顺序讲给别人听。 When I handle a business problem, I normally have a clear heading and a person responsible for it. My personal notebook is much more informal, which is probably why this takes me longer.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I recommend buying Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I will keep that in mind. I would like to keep the desk in this arrangement while we talk, because it finally feels less cluttered. 我发现纸一多，自己讲话也会跟着乱。不是没有想过整理，而是每次整理到一半，就有人进来问货到了没有，或者客户的邮件有没有回。 By the time I return, I put the papers into the nearest folder and tell myself I will sort them properly at home. Then at home I would rather sit with the family than open another folder.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: That sounds like a familiar tension between having a workable system and having time to maintain it. A personal folder does not need to look like an office archive to be useful. It might help to distinguish material you still want to read from material you are simply keeping, without attempting to reorganise everything at once. For our conversation, though, there is no need to solve the whole filing problem. Are you comfortable leaving the office calls with someone else while we speak, or should we allow for an interruption?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: My office manager can handle the calls. She knows I am on the telephone and will only knock if something really cannot wait. 平常我嘴上说让她处理，听见外面有动静还是会想出去看看。家里人也常说，我人在家里，耳朵还在仓库。今天我已经把门关上了，不然这通电话可能讲着讲着又变成讨论送货路线。 I am comfortable staying here. It is actually a relief to speak without having an open email window in front of me.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Then we can keep the focus here and leave the office manager to manage the room outside. There is something useful about a telephone conversation when you are accustomed to dealing with everything through a screen. You can look at the page that matters rather than at a queue of incoming messages. Before we return to the paperwork, I have a question from the background to our discussion. [[EV_001]]

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Let me find the sheet I put behind the notebook; I do not want to answer from the wrong page again. 这张纸的背面还有工作上的留言，我先把它翻过来。刚才进来的时候我只想着不要漏带东西，结果把不需要的东西也带来了。 There is an envelope here with my own handwriting on it, and that may be the one I was looking for. Give me a moment to lay it beside the book rather than on top of it.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Take your time with the envelope. There is no need to describe every sheet while you move it. If the office room is becoming cramped, you can keep the papers in a loose stack and bring forward only what you are reading. I will wait while you settle them. It is quite different from sitting at your usual desk, where you know where everything belongs without thinking about it. Here, even a familiar notebook can feel unfamiliar when the telephone and the correspondence are competing for space.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: That is true. At my own desk I can reach for something without looking, which is not necessarily the same as having a good system. 我父亲以前也是这样，桌面看起来很乱，可是别人碰一下，他马上就知道。现在我跟家里年轻的人一起做事，他们喜欢把文件放到共享的地方，我还会问原来的纸在哪里。 We have had some entertaining arguments about what counts as being organised. I am not opposed to their way; I just like being able to write a note in the margin.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: You can keep the margin notes without making the paper carry every part of the process. It is useful to separate your own working habits from the information that other people need to find. We can come back to the practical side of that later. I would like to cover the next part of our discussion now. [[EV_002]] [[EV_003]]

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: [[EV_004]] I would rather say that carefully than give you a quick conversational reply. 我讲话有时候会顺口接一句，尤其是电话里，对方还没讲完，我已经发出声音了。今天我想把该说的话讲清楚，不要只是因为怕电话里安静，就随便接话。 I am still sitting with the notebook open, but I am not writing while you are speaking.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: [[EV_007]] I will leave the pen down for the moment. 我以前接工作电话，总是一边听一边写，写到后来反而只顾着自己的字，没有留意对方下一句话。现在这样坐着听，跟平时在办公室接电话的感觉不太一样。 The door is still closed and nobody has come in, so we have a reasonably calm space to continue.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: We can leave the pen down and keep the conversation at this pace. You mentioned that the younger members of the family prefer shared records, while you prefer a page you can annotate. How does that work in the business from day to day? I am asking about the practical side of running the office rather than anything in your investment notebook. With deliveries and correspondence arriving throughout the day, I imagine there has to be a way for someone else to pick up an unfinished piece of work when you step away.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: There is, although it took us a while to make it feel natural. In the past, people would wait outside my office because they thought asking me was quicker than writing a clear note. 我后来发现，这样表面上很快，实际上所有事情都卡在我这里。我去吃饭，大家等我；我出门见客户，大家又等我。现在我们让负责的人把事情经过写下来，不只是留一句请回电。 The hard part was getting me to read their notes before asking them to tell the whole story again.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: That is an interesting distinction: a message saying that someone called does not give the next person much to work with. A brief account of what has already happened can prevent the same conversation being repeated around the office. It also means the person who handled the matter is not continually interrupted to reconstruct it from memory. Has the change made it easier for you to leave the premises when you have a family commitment, or do you still find yourself looking back at the office phone as you walk out?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I still look back, but less often. 我太太以前说，出门最慢的不是找停车位，而是等我走过办公室那条走廊。每经过一个人，我就停下来问一下，结果本来已经交代好的事情又讲一遍。现在她到楼下以后，我会让办公室的人直接提醒我下去，不要再开新的话题。 It sounds almost childish when I explain it, but a habit built around being available all the time is surprisingly hard to change. The staff have been more patient about it than I expected.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: It does not sound childish. A family business can make the line between being helpful and being permanently available quite hard to draw. A clear handover is different from disappearing without telling anyone, and your staff may appreciate knowing when you are genuinely off the desk. We can also keep this telephone conversation separate from the work waiting outside. If someone does need you, you can simply tell me you need a pause. You would not have to explain the whole office issue before stepping away from the handset.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: That is useful. At a branch I would be looking at the clock, wondering whether I had left enough time to get back. 在这里，我知道外面有人照看，也不用把文件装进包里再装出来。有时候去一个地方开会，真正讲话的时间不长，前后准备和路上花的心力反而很多。 I do not dislike seeing people in person. I just prefer a telephone conversation when the main task is to talk through papers that already live on my desk. I can find things more easily in familiar surroundings.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: That is a practical reason to use the telephone. An office visit has its place, but travelling with a bundle of loose papers can create its own work. Here you can leave the correspondence where it normally belongs and put it away when the call is over. It also helps if you are comfortable saying that you need a moment rather than trying to maintain a continuous conversation. Do you usually keep your personal correspondence at the office because that is where you spend most of the day, or does the notebook travel home with you?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: The notebook travels with me; the correspondence tends to stay at the office until I suddenly decide it should all go home. 然后家里的书桌就变成办公室的延伸。我太太不喜欢餐桌上放信封，这个我也觉得有道理，所以我给自己留了一个抽屉。问题是抽屉关上以后，看起来整齐了，我就不再记得里面还有东西等着看。 I am good at remembering a conversation with a customer, but not always good at remembering an unopened envelope once it has vanished from sight.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: A closed drawer can remove the visual reminder without removing the task. You might prefer an open tray for unread correspondence and a separate place for material you are keeping after reading it. That is only an organisational suggestion, not a need to create a complicated home office. The important distinction is whether something still needs your attention. A folder of finished correspondence and an envelope you have not opened may look equally tidy in a drawer, but they represent very different things when you sit down to deal with them.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, that is the distinction I tend to lose. 我整理的时候，很在意桌面是不是干净，反而没有想清楚哪些事情还没做完。有时把纸收走，心里就觉得事情也收好了。到了晚上想起来，又不想把抽屉翻乱。 A tray could work if I keep it away from the dining table. I do not want every meal to come with a visible reminder of correspondence. Perhaps the corner of the study would be better, where I can leave things without spreading them across the whole room.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: The study sounds more separate from family time. It may also help to give the tray a plain label that describes its purpose rather than the subject of every letter. Otherwise you can end up building an elaborate set of categories that takes longer to maintain than the correspondence itself. Do the other people at home use that desk as well? I ask because a shared surface often works better when everyone knows which pile is active and which papers can be moved without disturbing someone's unfinished work.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: My wife uses it occasionally, mostly for household correspondence, and the children leave things there when they visit. 所以也不能完全按我的习惯来安排。以前我会说不要碰我的纸，可是大家都住在同一个家里，总不能每个角落都变成我的工作区域。现在我尽量把自己的东西放在可以整个拿走的文件夹里，别人需要桌面的时候，不必先问我每张纸该放哪里。 That has made the room more pleasant. It feels like part of the home again, rather than a room everyone else has to tiptoe around.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: A folder that can be lifted away is a simple way to make a shared desk genuinely shared. It also avoids turning a family member into the custodian of your filing habits. When you come back to the desk, your papers are still together, and no one has had to decide what is important on your behalf. You mentioned earlier that you like notes in the margin. Do you tend to write reminders to yourself, or are you recording the substance of conversations so you can return to them later?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Both, which is probably part of the trouble. A reminder might sit beside something somebody said, and later I cannot tell whether I was recording their words or my own thought. 我有时候会画箭头，从上面指到下面，又在旁边补一句。如果隔得久了，再看就像别人的笔记。工作上的本子已经比较规矩，因为同事可能要看；个人的本子我一直觉得只有自己看，不用那么正式。 This call has reminded me that being the only reader does not guarantee that I will remember what I meant.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: You could preserve the informal style while making the different uses visible. A heading such as a conversation note is different from a heading such as a reminder to yourself, even if the handwriting underneath is equally informal. There is no need to rewrite the old notebook during this call. For the future, a clear heading at the moment you write may be easier than trying to reconstruct the context later. Crossed arrows and additions make sense while a conversation is fresh, but they can become surprisingly difficult to follow after the surrounding day has faded.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: That is exactly it. I remember the atmosphere of a conversation much more readily than the order in which things were said. 有时我甚至记得当时谁站在门口、外面在下雨，可是纸上的箭头为什么画在那里，却想不起来。 I do not want to turn my notebook into formal minutes, but I could be clearer about whether a page is still being worked on. At the office, an unfinished draft has a visible place. At home, everything just becomes part of the same book.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Keeping the character of the notebook is reasonable. If the system becomes too formal, you may stop using it precisely when the day gets busy. A simple distinction between a working page and a page kept for reference could be enough for ordinary correspondence. You can also leave some space around a heading so later additions do not squeeze into every margin. When a page is completely full, the temptation is to add a note wherever there is room, even if the location makes its meaning less clear when you return to it.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: You have described my handwriting habits rather accurately. 我总觉得空白留着有点浪费，所以会把能写的地方都写满。后来连自己都找不到句子的开头。年轻的时候跑客户，手里只有一个小本子，这样写很方便；现在坐在办公室，有整张纸可以用，习惯却还没有改。 I used to take a certain pride in fitting everything onto a page. Now I suspect I would be better served by leaving room to breathe. There is a difference between carrying less paper and making the paper useful.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: That distinction applies to email as well. A very short message is not necessarily a clear message if it leaves the reader guessing what has happened. In a family business, do people prefer to call across the room rather than write, or has most of the internal correspondence moved onto screens? I am interested in how you manage the practical handover. You have described an office where people know each other well, and that familiarity can make an informal exchange feel sufficient even when someone absent will need the context later.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: It depends on the person. Some people write a very clear message; others send a few words and assume I can reconstruct the whole day from them. 我以前也会这样，所以不能只怪同事。现在如果事情需要别人接手，我会请负责的人把经过写完整，尤其是已经跟客户讲过什么，不要让接电话的人又从头问起。 We are not trying to make ordinary office life bureaucratic. We are trying to stop the same unanswered question travelling from desk to desk while everyone thinks somebody else is dealing with it.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: That sounds like a useful boundary for the process: enough context for the next person, without a long report on every routine exchange. It can be frustrating when a message is technically recorded but not actually usable. A reader should be able to tell whether they need to do something or whether they are simply being kept informed. Have you found a comfortable way to mark that distinction in the business? It may be easier to borrow a habit that already works there than to invent a separate, elaborate system for your personal correspondence.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: We use plain headings now, and that helps. I resisted at first because I thought people would spend more time choosing a heading than doing the work, but the opposite happened. 大家知道哪些邮件要处理，哪些只是让人知道一下，就不会把所有东西都当成同样着急。我自己也慢慢少用那种只写请看附件的邮件，因为别人打开以后，还得猜我为什么发给他。 For personal papers I could use equally plain language. There is no prize for making the label clever if it stops being obvious when I am tired.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Plain language tends to survive a busy day better than a private code. It also helps if a folder has to be moved by someone else, because they can see what it is without reading the contents. You do not have to give other people access to the contents just to make the outside of the folder clear. For anything personal at the office, an obvious place of its own may prevent it from becoming mixed with delivery notes and customer letters. That would let you keep the convenience of your office desk without making all correspondence part of the business workflow.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I like that distinction. The office is convenient because I am here so much, but my private papers do not need to become office work. 我也不想同事为了帮我收拾桌子，反而要猜哪些东西能看、哪些不能碰。写清楚放在哪里，他们就不必替我判断内容。 I have sometimes brought a stack home and then brought it back unopened because I wanted the quieter desk at work. That is a lot of travelling for paper. A proper place here would be more sensible than pretending everything personal must always live at home.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: The place can follow the way you actually use the papers rather than an ideal routine that does not fit your week. It is also possible to keep a notebook portable while keeping the accompanying correspondence in a stable place. That way you are not carrying every envelope simply because it once sat beside the notebook. We have covered quite a lot of the practical background. If you want to return to the page you set aside at the start, you can do that now; I will give you a moment to find your place.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: The page is still open where I left it. [[EV_019]] [[EV_016]] I have kept the old pages covered, and that makes it much easier to stay with the current sheet. 我现在不用来回翻，只要把手边这张纸放平就可以。刚才讲整理文件的时候，我已经把旁边的信封移开了，桌面终于不像临时堆放的地方。 I will leave the business correspondence in the bag rather than try to sort it during our call.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: You can leave the bag closed. Trying to reorganise unrelated correspondence in the middle of a conversation would give you another task to keep in mind. We can continue with the page you have open and let the rest wait. Your description of moving paper between home and work made me wonder about the notebook itself: is it something you choose carefully, or is it simply whatever book happens to be available? People who rely on handwriting often have surprisingly definite preferences about the binding, the paper, or how flat the book stays on a desk.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I am quite particular about whether it lies flat. A book that keeps closing while I am on the telephone becomes irritating very quickly. 纸的颜色我倒不讲究，但不喜欢太滑，写起来没有感觉。装订太紧也不行，因为我会把电话放在旁边，一边看一边记，不能一直用手压着。 My wife teases me because I will spend ages choosing a notebook and then put completely unrelated things in it. She says I am very selective about the container and much less selective about the contents.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: That is a perceptive way to put it. The physical comfort of writing matters if the notebook is used throughout your day, but it cannot do the organising by itself. You may not need a different book so much as a more consistent way of starting a page. A heading and a little space can be easier to maintain than separate books that you might leave in different places. It depends on what you will actually carry. A beautifully organised notebook at home would not help much if all your handwritten reminders happen at the office.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Exactly. I tried separate books for different purposes, and then the one I wanted was always somewhere else. 最后还是写回随身带的本子，因为事情不会等我找到正确的封面才发生。与其要求自己每次拿对本子，不如在同一本里写清楚。 [[EV_017]] I have that part written in a clear space on the page, rather than squeezed into a margin. The page itself is not elegant, but at least it is no longer hidden under an envelope.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: There is no need for the page to be elegant. Being able to find and read it comfortably is more useful than making it look like a finished document. You can leave the older notebook habits alone for the rest of this conversation and think about changing them later. Sometimes a system works better when it is introduced at the next fresh page rather than imposed retrospectively on everything already written. Otherwise the organising project becomes large enough that it is difficult to begin, and the pile remains untouched.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: That is a sensible warning. I have a tendency to make a small household task into a project, especially if I can buy folders for it. 整理之前先想买什么，买回来又觉得应该等有空的时候全部做好，结果文件夹很整齐，纸还是原来的纸。家里人已经看穿这个过程了，所以现在我说要整理，他们就问我是不是只想去文具店。 I can laugh about it because they are not entirely wrong. Starting with the next blank page sounds less impressive, but much more likely to happen.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: It would also leave your free time intact. You spoke earlier about preferring to be with the family rather than opening another folder when you get home. A modest change that takes very little attention may be easier to keep than a large weekend sorting exercise. What do you enjoy doing together when you manage to leave office matters behind? There is no need for anything elaborate; sometimes the ordinary parts of an evening are precisely what get squeezed out when business correspondence follows someone through the front door.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Usually something very ordinary. Dinner without my phone beside the plate, or a walk where I do not stop to answer a message. 我以前觉得这些事情随时都可以做，所以总把工作放前面。后来发现，如果一直说等忙完再说，家里的人就一直在等。现在我会尽量在回家之前把需要交代的事情讲清楚，免得吃饭的时候又临时打回办公室。 We still talk about the business at home because it is part of the family, but I am trying not to make it the only subject available.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: A family business can provide an endless supply of conversation, especially when everyone recognises the people and the situations involved. It can be difficult to notice that the whole evening has become an informal office meeting. Leaving space for other subjects does not require pretending the business does not exist. It might simply mean letting someone finish a story that has nothing to do with work before you return to your own day. Does your family usually notice before you do when the conversation has drifted back towards the office?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Immediately. They have a much better ear for it than I do. 我有时候只是提到一个熟人，就顺着讲到他的订单，再讲到办公室发生的事情，自己完全没有觉得转了话题。太太会笑着问，这个故事最后是不是又要讲送货。我听到才发现，还真是。 We are better at catching it without turning it into an argument now. Nobody is asking me to become a different person; they just want some room in the evening for things that do not have to be followed up the next morning.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: That seems a constructive way to handle it. A gentle reminder can preserve the evening more easily than waiting until everyone is frustrated. The same principle can apply to office handovers: a clear stopping point lets people know that they are not expected to keep the conversation running indefinitely. We can use pauses here in the same ordinary way. You have your page in front of you, and there is no need to keep writing while we talk. If you want a moment to look at it again, please take that moment.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I am looking at it now. [[EV_018]] The handwriting is clearer here because I wrote this sitting at a desk, not standing beside the loading area. 我有些笔记真的是站着写的，纸下面垫着信封，难怪后来自己也认不出来。今天这些纸带进来之前，我还以为只要找到本子就够了。现在觉得，把写字的地方选好，也比事后努力辨认省事。 I will keep the page flat and avoid adding anything else in the margins while we finish talking.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Writing while standing in a busy area does ask a lot of a small notebook. It is understandable that a quick reminder looks different from something written at a settled desk. You need not make every working note permanent; some are simply there to help you get back to a task. The difficulty comes when a temporary scribble is kept alongside correspondence without any indication of its role. A little separation at the end of the day might be more useful than trying to write perfectly while someone is waiting for you near the loading area.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I like that because it leaves room for the way the business actually works. 有时候事情就在现场发生，不可能请大家停下来，等我坐好再写。可是回到办公室以后，可以把临时记的东西看一下，不要直接把本子合起来。以前我把合上本子当作事情告一段落，其实只是把问题盖住了。 I do not need a perfect record of every ordinary exchange. I need to stop treating a hurried reminder as if its meaning will remain obvious forever. That is a manageable habit to work on.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: A manageable habit is usually easier to keep during a busy week. You can also avoid asking your memory to do two jobs at once: remembering the task and remembering how the shorthand was meant to be read. In your office, is there already a quiet point when you review what remains on the desk, or does leaving tend to happen in response to the next appointment? I am thinking only of the practical routine. A habit is often easier to attach to something you already do than to a new reminder that becomes another piece of correspondence.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Leaving used to happen whenever someone reminded me I was late. Now I try to clear the desk enough that I can see what is still active. 我不一定把所有事情做完，但至少知道哪些留给同事，哪些等我回来。这个动作本来就有，只是以前只管工作文件，没有看自己的本子。顺手翻一下，应该比另设一个提醒自然。 I would rather connect it to closing the office door than give myself another notification. My phone already has enough reasons to light up without becoming a supervisor for my notebook.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: That makes sense as a practical preference. A reminder can stop being useful if it becomes part of the background noise of the day. Since you already have a desk routine, there may be no need to add a new device or application. You can keep the arrangement as simple as the notebook and the place you leave it. We can stay with the telephone today in much the same spirit: no need to turn the conversation into a technology project when what you wanted was time to work through the papers you already had.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I appreciate that. Whenever someone says there is an application for organising something, I wonder whether I am about to acquire another thing that needs organising. 我不是不愿意学，只是工具多了以后，资料会分散。我在手机里存一点，在电脑上放一点，最后还是回到纸上找。 [[EV_020]] That is on the same clear page in front of me. I will leave the computer closed, because opening it now would only invite me to check the office messages.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: The computer can stay closed. We do not need to bring the office inbox into the room just because it is within reach. A telephone conversation is often more comfortable when there is a clear physical boundary around it, even if that boundary is only a closed laptop and a closed door. You mentioned that you prefer longer calls to trying to fit everything into a branch visit. Is that partly because you like having room to return to a point after you have thought about it, rather than treating the conversation as a list to get through?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Very much so. I often remember the useful question after the conversation has already moved on. 电话里可以说，刚才那个地方我想再讲一下，不用担心是不是打乱了别人安排好的见面时间。当然我也知道不能一直绕，所以今天尽量让纸放在原来的位置，免得每次回头又从头找。 In business meetings I can be quite direct because the subject is familiar and someone usually has an agenda. With personal papers, I need a little more room to gather my thoughts and notice what I have left unfinished.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Returning to a point is not a problem in itself. It is easier to follow when we make the transition clear rather than letting a thought from earlier slip into the middle of another subject. We have been able to keep the practical conversation separate from the page you are reading, which helps. You do not have to imitate the pace of a business meeting. At the same time, I can keep my own questions concise so you are not trying to hold a long question in mind while searching through the notebook.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Concise questions help. 我平常接电话，有人前面铺垫很久，等真正的问题出来，我可能还在想他前面说的背景。尤其手上有纸的时候，很容易看着一个词就走神。所以我宁愿你讲得直接一点，需要找东西的时候，我就说我在找。 That seems more courteous than making conversational noises while I am actually reading. I am trying to get better at letting a pause be a pause. It is not something that came naturally when I first started dealing with customers by telephone.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Many people feel a need to fill a silence on the telephone because there is no visible indication that the other person is reading or thinking. Saying that you are looking for a page is enough to explain the pause. We can then avoid speaking over each other or mistaking a sound made while searching for a response. You have been clear about what you are doing at the desk. There is still no need to tidy everything before the call ends; the unrelated papers can remain in the bag until you have a suitable moment for them.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: The bag can wait. The room is much calmer with it closed. 我刚才进来还想着，讲完电话可以顺便把所有信件整理好，现在觉得不必把事情绑在一起。每次都想顺便多做一点，最后反而不知道自己原来要做什么。 I have a tendency to bring that business habit home as well: if I am already at the desk, I think I should use the opportunity to clear every task nearby. Then an ordinary evening becomes an unexpectedly long session of sorting things nobody asked me to sort.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: It can be useful to give a task a stopping point that is not defined by the entire desk being empty. Otherwise the surrounding correspondence keeps expanding what you meant to do. For this call, you can leave the room as it is when we finish and decide later where the papers belong. You do not need a completely new routine before you can put the notebook away. You have already made the immediate workspace easier to use by keeping the older pages covered and the unrelated bag closed.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: That small change has helped more than I expected. 我以前总觉得整理一定要做得彻底，才算是真的整理。其实今天只是把不需要看的东西挪开，讲话已经顺畅多了。回家以后我也可以先让桌面只留正在看的东西，不必马上决定每张旧纸最后放哪里。 I may still return to earlier points in conversation, but at least I will not be physically returning to the wrong pile each time. There is a difference between thinking something over and losing my place among envelopes.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: There is, and keeping the physical place stable makes the conversation easier to follow. Before I move to the next part, you can make sure you are comfortable and that the handset is not pulling against the papers. We have been speaking for a while, so there is no need to hold an awkward position just to keep the notebook open. If you have put the pen down, it can remain down. I will speak clearly, and you can leave the correspondence where it is rather than trying to write at the same time.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I have moved the handset to the other side of the book, which is better. The cord was catching the corner whenever I turned my head. 以前这间房主要拿来放样本，后来才加了桌子，所以插座和电话的位置不太顺手。平时短短讲几句不会觉得，坐久了才发现手一直悬着。 It is still more comfortable than balancing the papers in the car between appointments. I used to tell myself that was efficient, but it mostly meant I arrived everywhere with loose sheets on the passenger seat.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: A settled desk is certainly easier for handling loose correspondence than a passenger seat. It also means you can leave the papers undisturbed if we need a pause. We have worked through the page and the surrounding conversation, and I will now read the complete instruction back. [[EV_008]]

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: [[EV_009]] The supporting papers may be in the sleeve behind the notebook rather than in the bag. 我先找一下，不想又拿错。刚才为了把桌面腾出来，我把信封都放在同一边，现在要看看里面夹的是哪一张。 Please leave me a little quiet while I look; I am finding that easier than trying to talk and read together.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I will leave you some quiet. You do not need to describe the search as you go, and I will not keep adding questions while you are reading. Keep the notebook where it is if that helps you avoid losing the page. The supporting material can come out of its sleeve separately; there is no need to spread every envelope across the desk again. I am still here on the line, so you can simply speak when you have finished looking rather than checking whether I am waiting.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I have found a paper that reminds me of something I have not mentioned. 这部分我应该直接讲，不要夹在文件里让人猜。我先把纸放下来，免得一边找一边说，讲得又不完整。 [[EV_010]] I had been concentrating on the notebook and the way I had arranged everything on the desk. That is why I am bringing this up now rather than continuing to search through the envelopes.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Thank you for telling me. I will leave the conversation there for now rather than continue through the papers today. You can keep the notebook and the supporting material together, and there is no need to reorganise them while we are still on the line. I appreciate you taking the time to speak. We can end the call here, and you can return to the office when you are ready rather than trying to attend to the room outside while holding the handset. Thank you, Adrian.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Thank you, Clara. I will put the papers back in their sleeve before I open the door. 今天讲了很久，外面倒是一直很安静，看来办公室并没有因为我关门讲话就停下来。这一点我回去以后也该记住，不要一出门就把所有事情重新问一遍。 I will leave the unrelated correspondence in the bag and take the notebook with me. Thank you for giving me room to find the pages without hurrying me through them. Goodbye.
